messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int i = 0;
while (i < 4) { fire(); }

Question: How many shots are fired?
The student answered: 4

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: The loop variable advances by itself and the loop ends by itself

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: sure of themselves, plain English, one sentence of 8 to 18 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["The loop runs while i is less than four, so it fires four times before i reaches four.", "Since i starts at zero and the condition checks i less than four, four shots happen.", "The value of i keeps moving ahead each round until it hits four and then stops.", "Every repeat of the loop counts as one shot, and there are four repeats because of the limit four.", "i goes up on its own inside the loop, so after four shots it becomes four and the loop finishes."]}

sentences: The loop runs while i is less than four, so it fires four times before i reaches four.
Since i starts at zero and the condition checks i less than four, four shots happen.
The value of i keeps moving ahead each round until it hits four and then stops.
Every repeat of the loop counts as one shot, and there are four repeats because of the limit four.
i goes up on its own inside the loop, so after four shots it becomes four and the loop finishes.
